# Edva language reference

Edva is expression-oriented: bindings, calls, choices, cycles, and blocks are
formed from expressions. Indentation creates blocks, and the language has no
reserved keywords. This is the reader-facing map of the language; individual
pages state the current rules and point to their implementation and test
evidence.

The operator table in `GRAMMAR.md` is generated from
`operators.yaml`. It is the sole precedence table; the pages below
explain use and constraints rather than maintaining a competing copy.

## At a glance

| Area | Main forms |
|---|---|
| source | UTF-8, indentation blocks, `//` and `/* ... */` comments |
| bindings | `name = value`, `name' = replacement`, `::name = global` |
| functions | `f: T => U`, `f = value => body`, `f(argument)` |
| modules | `#use name`, `#use path/module`, `module::name`, `#public`, `#private` |
| branching | `value [case] body | fallback` |
| iteration | `iterable @ item => body`, `-->`, `--^`, `>--` |
| composite values | records, growable arrays, maps, rams, enums |
| compile time | `#!`, `#! T: Type`, `#size(Type)` |
| interop | `#foreign`, `#export`, `Addr`, `&builder`, `&string` |
